On startup, rapache behaves a bit differently than R:

rApache doesn't source profiles of any kind, neither site nor user. R does. Implication being a reduced library path, so that's why users report rapache not finding a library when user installs it from command line R.

rApache's working directory is typically a place where the web server cannot write files, so it is up to the user to manage where files are stored. users should also not presume the working directory they set will be set on each web request.

rapache processes share one temporary directory, so its important that users create unique file names.

Jeff

That looks like poor design, who gave you this idea? :-) Better is to
store images outside of /var/www/ with a unique identifier and have an
R script that sends those images dynamically. E.g if your application
generates a PNG file, you could store it in /tmp with some random uuid
as filename. E.g. /tmp/a7e9c290-cd2e-11e1-9b23-0800200c9a66.

Then you pass on the uuid to the client through ajax or so, and you
expose an R script through rapache that can be used to retrieve the
images. Something like this:

## begin getimages.R

uuid <- GET$uuid;
filename <- file.path("/tmp", uuid);
stopifnot(file.exists(filename))

setContentType(type='image/png')
sendBin(object=readBin(filename,'raw',n=file.info <http://file.info>(filename)$size))

## end R script

The client can than go to .e.g
http://something.com/R-files/getimages.R?uuid=a7e9c290-cd2e-11e1-9b23-0800200c9a66
and will get the image.

messages.body_plain:
All,

I'm planning on bumping the minor number to 2, e.g. the next release
will be 1.2.0 because...

1.2.0 will set the working directory to a sensible place when using
RFileEval, RFileHandler, or r-script.

For instance with a Rook deployment like this:

 <Location /hmisc>
        SetHandler r-handler
        RFileEval "/home/hornerj/Hmisc/config.R:Rook::Server$call(app)"
</Location>

It makes sense to change the working directory to
"/home/hornerj/Hmisc". That way, the examples in the Rook package can
work without change.

Also, for:

<Directory /home/hornerj/rapache/test/brew>
  SetHandler r-script
  RHandler brew::brew
</Directory>

and a request of  /home/hornerj/rapache/test/brew/simple.html, it
makes sense to set the working directory to
"/home/hornerj/rapache/test/brew". Or if the request was
/home/hornerj/rapache/test/brew/subdir/foo.html, it makes sense to set
it to /home/hornerj/rapache/test/brew/subdir.

Comments?

Jeff
